cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Newcomer – A person who has recently arrived in a place or joined a group.

p.em: Example: The arrival of a newcomer at the law firm threatens the established social dynamic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Suspicion – A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true.

p.em: Example: The office staff treats the replacement character with hilarious suspicion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Meta – Self-referential; referring to itself or the conventions of its genre.

p.em: Example: The song is brilliantly meta, mocking television recasting and new cast additions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disrupt – To interrupt an event, activity, or process by causing a disturbance or problem.

p.em: Example: A new employee can completely disrupt the delicate balance of office gossip.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dynamic – The forces or properties that stimulate growth or change within a system or group.

p.em: Example: Adding a new person alters the emotional dynamic of the entire group.

cosy-blockquote.p: Replacement – A person or thing that takes the place of another.

p.em: Example: Nobody likes feeling like an unwanted replacement for a beloved friend.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gossip – Casual or unconstrained conversation or reports about other people.

p.em: Example: Office gossip spikes whenever a mysterious new guy walks through the door.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intruder – A person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

p.em: Example: They initially view Scott as an unwelcome intruder invading their song routines.

cosy-blockquote.p: Resentment – Bitter indignation at having been treated unfairly.

p.em: Example: Unearned resentment builds up when team members fear losing their standing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Integration – The action or process of integrating or combining into an equal group.

p.em: Example: Successful integration into a tight-knit workplace takes time and effort.

Incorrect: They are suspicious about the newcomer → Correct: They are suspicious of the newcomer ((Use 'suspicious of'.))
Incorrect: He tried to integrate to the team → Correct: He tried to integrate into the team ((Use 'integrate into' a group or team.))
